flags.summary: Prospect volunteered drug use alongside heavy alcohol use as the worst part of his habits; the rep acknowledged the honesty, never asked a single follow-up question, and proceeded to build a nutrition and accountability plan that addresses alcohol only.
evidence: I don't eat, the worst thing is alcohol, the worst thing is alcohol, and some drugs.
The worst thing is alcohol consumption. Okay. — Alcohol is the main thing we need to work on.
And then he's also going to help you stay accountable to not drinking as much. He's going to check in with you on that part.

flags.summary: After the $6,000 offer was refused the rep introduced an unpublished tier at $1,000 for six months, neither of the two sanctioned prices.
evidence: We have an investment of 6k USD for six months.

flags.summary: Two irreconcilable monthly prices were quoted for the same $1,000 six-month product within about ninety seconds — $200 a month and then $600 a month — and neither was corrected before the call ended with the prospect going away to discuss the cost with his wife.
evidence: That is 1,000 for six months. We can also do 200 a month, but that's sort of throwing away 200. So yeah, it's up to you.
Yeah, so it's 1,000 for six months. If you want to do it per month, it would be $600 a month.

flags.summary: Rep dismissed the prospect's own pre-call price research on the cheaper product as 'something completely different', then sold him that same product four turns later.
evidence: I'll be honest. I searched online, and then after, and I thought there was something like $200.
I would say what you saw online, because I know what you're talking about, that that's something completely different.
